issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the feeding-sound method using two different names: the UML and many tasks specify an abstract method messageOnFeed(), but several specific animal tasks and the song template refer to getFeedingSound(). The solution and intended design use messageOnFeed(). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and which name to call when composing the song verse.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement, template, and tests. Preferably update the problem text and example song to use messageOnFeed() everywhere (or, if getFeedingSound() is preferred, rename the abstract method and all implementations in template/solution to getFeedingSound()). Also update any example placeholders in the song to refer to the chosen method name.

issues.description: The problem statement alternates between two method names for the animal feeding sound: the UML and tasks specify an abstract method messageOnFeed(), and both the template/solution code expect/implement messageOnFeed(), but several places in the problem text (e.g. instructions for Seal/Pig/Goat and the feedAllAnimals description) incorrectly refer to getFeedingSound(). This naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (returning the feeding sound) can confuse students about which method to implement and call, and may lead to incorrect implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent with the UML and code by replacing all references to getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed(), or vice versa (preferably messageOnFeed() to match the UML and provided solution). Update the description lines (Seal/Pig/Goat instructions and feedAllAnimals description) so students have a single, unambiguous method name to implement and call.
